name: pointer-highlight
title: Pointer Highlight
description: Wraps a line of text in a thin rectangle that draws itself when it scrolls into view, with a little click cursor landing at the bottom-right corner in a colour you choose.
use: A short line in a hero should feel pointed at, as if someone circled it in a design review.
avoid: It draws once and stays: there is no hover response despite the cursor glyph, so it cannot stay interactive.
a11y: The border and cursor are purely decorative, and the draw animation ignores reduced-motion. (keyboard: n-a, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Three short lines of white text on black, each inside a thin rectangular outline with sharp corners. A small arrow cursor sits just outside each box's bottom-right corner, two blue and one green.
behaves: When the text scrolls into view the border grows out from the corner while a cursor fades in and slides to the bottom-right, then everything holds still.
customise: Wrap the content and recolour the box and arrow with rectangleClassName and pointerClassName; draw timing and cursor placement are in the source.
weight: light: Two short draw animations per wrapped block, fired once when it enters view.
demo: Lines 'Ship faster than ever', 'Build beautiful interfaces with zero friction' and 'Open source · MIT license'.
issues: While the border is drawing, the cursor arrow sits on top of the words and reads as an overlap.
polishWhy: Crisp, well-timed box with a charming cursor; the arrow overlaps the text while drawing.
